articles.title: International Film Festival Rotterdam Names Pepijn Kuyper Managing Director, Succeeding Clare Stewart
articles.summary: "His experience in the commercial elements of cultural organizations and deep connections with the Dutch film ecosystem are a fantastic fit for us," says the Dutch festival.
articles.content:
The International Film Festival Rotterdam (IFFR) has appointed Pepijn Kuyper as its new managing director, succeeding Clare Stewart. He will join IFFR in mid-January 2027 and work alongside Stewart during a handover period through the conclusion of the 2027 edition of the festival, which runs Jan. 28- Feb. 7.

Kuyper is currently managing director of Amerpodia, which operates three cultural institutions in Amsterdam, namely Rode Hoed in a former church, Felix Meritis and De Nieuwe Liefde in a former warehouse.

"Kuyper is an experienced cultural leader who brings his film sector expertise, networks, and a track record in cultural entrepreneurship to his new role at IFFR," the fest said. His career spans work for film and cultural organizations in Rotterdam, Utrecht, Nijmegen, and Amsterdam. Among other roles, he previously served as business director at the Netherlands Film Festival. Before that, he served as managing director of LUX in Nijmegen and LantarenVenster in Rotterdam, both venues for multidisciplinary programming of film, debate, music and media. At LantarenVenster, a longstanding IFFR venue, he helped establish year-round collaborations with the festival.

I’m looking forward to working alongside him and the team, building on what we have developed together and continuing to create opportunities for filmmakers and audiences."

And Kuyper himself shared: “As a Rotterdammer, I have followed IFFR from a young age, first as a visitor and later through my professional roles in film and culture. I have seen first-hand what the festival means to filmmakers, audiences and the cultural life of the city."

British filmmaker and actress Louise Connelly-Burnham has signed with CAA .

Connolly-Burnham wrote, directed and produced "The Intimacy Coordinator," an erotic thriller currently on the international festival circuit and qualified for both the Oscars and BAFTAs. The short film, which won best director at HollyShorts, best actress at FilmQuest and the Women in Film Award at Flickers’ Rhode Island International Film Festival, sees her play an intimacy coordinator who is also a sex addict. Prior to "The Intimacy Coordinator," Connolly-Burnham wrote, directed and produced "Sister Wives," in which she starred alongside Mia McKenna-Bruce ("How to Have Sex," "Agatha Christie's Seven Dials"). The short, which follows two women who fall in love within a fundamentalist polygamous community, won more than 50 awards, including the Iris Prize for best British short and Hollyshort's best director and best LGBTQIA+ film, and was longlisted for the BAFTAs and BIFAs. Film4 acquired the "Sisters Wives," which ranked No. 3 among short films in Letterboxd’s 2024 Global Year in Review.

A feature adaptation of "Sister Wives" is now in development with American Zoetrope, the famed production company founded by Francis Ford Coppola and George Lucas. "The Intimacy Coordinator" is also being developed for a feature film adaptation.

articles.title: Avengers: Doomsday Should Set Up This X-Men Character to Lead Into the 2028 Reboot
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Even though some fans have balked at the lack of a formal build-up to the MCU’s Doctor Doom, the marketing for Avengers: Doomsday has certainly succeeded in making the film feel like an event. The arrival of a character as iconic and powerful as Doom deserves nothing less, and uniting the disparate teams of the […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Even though some fans have balked at the lack of a formal build-up to the MCU’s Doctor Doom , the marketing for Avengers: Doomsday has certainly succeeded in making the film feel like an event. The arrival of a character as iconic and powerful as Doom deserves nothing less, and uniting the disparate teams of the Multiverse Saga — the Avengers, the New Avengers, the Wakandans, the Fantastic Four, and Fox’s X-Men — definitely qualifies as such. Of course, the stakes feel particularly heavy for the latter team, seeing as Marvel Studios is well into planning a franchise reboot for release in 2028 .

So the Fox era of the X-Men, which launched with the original film in 2000 and carries into 2024’s Deadpool & Wolverine , is all but finished. But what remains a mystery is exactly how those versions of these characters will be put to rest. By the looks of it, the X-Men’s Earth-10005 is about to meet its end due to an incursion in Avengers: Doomsday . But there’s talk that at least some of the mutant heroes could live to fight another day before the new cast steps in. If that’s the case, there’s only one X-Men character who should carry out that storyline.

When he debuted as Scott Summers aka Cyclops in 2000’s X-Men , James Marsden had only appeared in a handful of movies, most notably the 1998 sci-fi horror film Disturbing Behavior opposite Katie Holmes. However, he certainly looked the part, and so X-Men fans generally embraced the casting. But it didn’t take long for the backlash to kick in. This wasn’t due to Marsden’s performance but rather how underused Cyclops was in that initial trilogy. After the first film’s focus on Wolverine and Rogue, the sequels saw Cyclops slip increasingly into the background. And in the end, his character was killed off-screen early in X-Men: The Last Stand , freeing Marsden up for a supporting role in the same year’s Superman Returns .

With the Multiverse Saga, though, Marvel Studios has taken this chance to circle back to many of the pre-MCU Marvel movies. And though the Doomsday clock is ticking, the latest Avengers movie has the chance to finally do right by Marsden’s Cyclops . Despite often being depicted as the field leader of the X-Men, Cyclops has rarely been able to fulfill that role onscreen or demonstrate the full power of his optic blast. X-Men ‘97 only further emphasized how poorly the films handled the character, but Avengers: Doomsday could see Marsden call “To me, my X-Men” in a mutant-filled moment akin to Avengers: Endgame ’s iconic “Avengers, assemble.” Furthermore, if rumors are true, and Cyclops survives into Avengers: Secret War s, then he could be the one to put that final touches on the era of Fox’s X-Men franchise.

Although little is officially confirmed about the plot of Avengers: Secret Wars , fans strongly believe it will follow a select group of surviving heroes from the multiverse into Doom’s Battleworld. Beyond that film, we know that the MCU will be consolidated back into just one universe, setting the stage for a new era of X-Men. But Avengers: Secret Wars also presents the chance for Kit Connor to debut his own version of Scott Summers, perhaps even coming face to face with Marsden’s version of the character. Following the introduction of Sadie Sink’s Jean Grey in Spider-Man: Brand New Day , it makes sense that Connor’s Cyclops would get his own intro, putting two of Charles Xavier’s top students on equal narrative footing prior to the X-Men team film.

Having both Marsden and Connor in the same film could lead to a scenario in which Marsden’s Cyclops chooses to sacrifice himself to save his MCU variant. Imagine a scene in which the elder Cyclops realizes that his time has passed and hands over the future of the X-Men franchise to Connor’s Scott Summers. This would give the Fox era of X-Men films to a powerful close, serving as meta-commentary but also giving the new Cyclops a burden to carry. Armed with the knowledge of his destined role within the X-Men, the new Cyclops would already feel the pressure of leadership and the need to earn his spot among this new generation of mutants. Much like Jean Grey’s past trauma informs her future, so too can this new Cyclops be propelled forward with a very relatable chip on his shoulder. But of course, this is all pure speculation.

Would you like to see James Marsden hand over the X-Men franchise to Kit Connor in Avengers: Secret Wars ? Sound off with your thoughts in the comments section below!

Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters on December 18, 2026.

The controversial " Netflix tax" could raise up to £1.6B ($2.1B) for the BBC within six years, according to new research.

Ampere Analysis modeled how the plan to force those who watch streamers' non-live content to pay the £180 annual licence fee even if they don't watch the BBC could make a difference to the corporation's coffers.

Billy Porter and Hannah John-Kamen have boarded as producers on " The Colour of My Skin ," a short film co-directed by Anuparna Roy, who took the Horizons best director prize at the 2025 Venice Film Festival, and British-Indian activist, curator and artist Amar Singh. Filming has wrapped.

Porter and John-Kamen produce with Stephanie Faucher and Jordan Dykstra. Studio Á, the art and film studio Singh co-founded with Dykstra, is also on board. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Prime Video, RTP Take Portuguese Rights to ‘Gisberta,’ Leonel Vieira’s True-Crime Docuseries BMG’s Concord Originals Preps Supernatural Gothic Horror Pic ‘Wolf at the Door’ (EXCLUSIVE)

Singh wrote the screenplay and stars opposite Efeosa Jordan Afolabi and Namita Lal.

The story centers on Avi, a British-Indian artist getting ready to show his work at an art salon, and Darius, a Black musician with whom he has a fraught romantic past.

Art, ambition and unresolved feelings draw Avi and Darius into each other's orbit. The film uses that collision to probe racial identity, colonial history and equality, and the awkward gap between the ideals people defend in public and how they behave behind closed doors.

The short reunites Singh with Roy. He was an associate producer on her second feature, "Lovers in the Blue Night," which won the Netpac Award for best Asian film at the 2026 Venice Film Festival.

A year earlier, Roy's debut feature, "Songs of Forgotten Trees," earned her the Horizons directing prize at Venice, making her the first Indian filmmaker to win it.

"I believe the political often becomes most visible in these intimate moments, when love and our personal convictions come into conflict," Roy said.

The film grows out of a poem Singh wrote, also titled "The Colour of My Skin," which grapples with the lasting legacy of colonialism, racial inequality, displacement and the longing to belong. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"For years at Amar Gallery, I have tried to bring attention to artists and stories that have been overlooked. Making this film gave me the opportunity to turn some of those questions inward. I wanted to explore whether the values we defend through art are always reflected in the way we treat the people closest to us. It's a story about identity and injustice, but also about love, contradiction and what it means to truly see another person," Singh said.

At his London gallery, Singh has spotlighted female, minority and LGBTQ+ artists the art world long ignored, using exhibitions and cultural programs to push back against its accepted narratives. His human rights work outside the gallery includes the campaign to decriminalize homosexuality in India, as well as efforts to improve women's rights and representation in cultural institutions.

Sunil Borkar shot the film, and Maximillian Raynor designed the costumes.

"The Colour of My Skin" is now heading into post-production. The news was unveiled on the sidelines of the WAVES Film Bazaar , the market arm of the International Film Festival of India in Goa.

articles.title: 3 Cult Classic ’80s Movies You Couldn’t Make in 2026 (But Pop Culture Needed Them)
articles.summary: People got away with a lot of nonsense in the 1980s. Racism, misogyny, and homophobia were rampant in film and television. Thankfully, the tide has since turned, and there is much less tolerance for bigotry in media today. That said, the 1980s also yielded some incredible films that tackled important subject matter. Regardless of how […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google People got away with a lot of nonsense in the 1980s. Racism, misogyny, and homophobia were rampant in film and television. Thankfully, the tide has since turned, and there is much less tolerance for bigotry in media today. That said, the 1980s also yielded some incredible films that tackled important subject matter. Regardless of how uncomfortable it can be, dark, potentially offensive, dark, or cynical art is sometimes the best way to probe the reasons behind our behaviors, find catharsis in our societal problems, and even understand the villains and perpetrators behind them.

Today, we’ve reached a point in culture where nearly every big studio movie gets filtered through numerous focus groups and is often sanitized of any edge that could make anyone uncomfortable. That means some of the most iconic ’80s films, particularly midnight movies and cult classics, would never have been made today unless a rogue independent studio stuck its neck out for them. Nonetheless, these films are essential not only to film history, but to pop culture and culture at large. The films on this list likely wouldn’t get the green light now, but it’s worth asking why and considering the positive impacts they’ve had.

Directed by Michael Lehmann and starring Winona Ryder and Christian Slater, Heathers follows high schooler Veronica, who is part of her school’s ruthless “Heathers” clique. As she becomes disgusted by their cruelty, she simultaneously falls for the rebel JD, and their attempts to humble the popular kids escalate into staging suicides and a plot to blow up the school. The climax centers on JD wiring the school’s boiler room with explosives to kill the entire student body during a pep rally. In a post-Columbine world, however, a comedic school bombing likely wouldn’t make it past a first draft. Additionally, the duo repeatedly murders popular kids and stages their deaths as suicides, making suicide seem cool and trendy among the teens.

Yet despite satirizing some particularly dark themes, the film has retained a devoted audience of fans who love it because it weaponizes its taboos to expose hypocrisy. Heathers relies on its shocking premise to skewer how adults, the media, and even peers might exploit tragedy for clout. It’s also important to film history because it broke John Hughes’ mold of writing teens with earnest sentimentality, moving instead into a more cynical, postmodern place. Without it, there would be no Mean Girls , no Jennifer’s Body , and no Euphoria .

Written and directed by Bruce Robinson and starring Richard E. Grant and Paul McGann, Withnail and I is a British cult classic that spins a yarn about two unemployed actors: Withnail and Marwood, as they escape their squalid flat for a weekend at a country cottage owned by Withnail’s Uncle Monty. Yet, it would never get past the censors today, primarily because its central dramatic tension relies on what would now be considered a predatory gay stereotype. Uncle Monty is an older gay man who relentlessly pursues Marwood after Withnail lies and presents Marwood as gay and interested. Modern audiences would likely spit this out, for good reason, as it portrays the older queer character as a persistent sexual predator. Additionally, its overtone of bleak nihilism amounts to essentially zero conventional moral growth by the end of the film, which is rarely seen today, particularly in major studio films.

Still, the merit of Withnail and I lies in its honest portrayal of creative failure. Whereas Hollywood stories often see struggling artists eventually getting their big break, Withnail and I captures the bottomless pit of watching talent go unrecognized. Its bittersweet ending, in which Withnail recites Hamlet to wolves in the rain, is a beautiful tableau of the lonely artist’s plight. A blueprint for British comedy, its hilarious, rapid-fire dialogue and celebration of glorious losers directly influenced modern UK comedies like Peep Show and Shaun of the Dead . Even though the Uncle Monty plot is dated, the film treats Monty’s grief and loneliness with empathy, and stereotypes aside, Withnail and I remains an essential piece of the British film canon.

Written and directed by auteur David Lynch, Blue Velvet revolves around college student Jeffrey (Kyle MacLachlan), whose amateur investigation leads him down a rabbit hole into the sadomasochistic suburban underworld controlled by Dennis Hopper’s Frank Booth, who has kidnapped the family of nightclub singer Dorothy (Isabella Rossellini). It wouldn't be made today because some of the film’s most memorable set pieces depict graphic sexual violence, with Frank assaulting Dorothy. It was a difficult watch even for its time, with Roger Ebert famously condemning Blue Velvet for how it degraded Rossellini (though she still defends it to this day). Jeffrey also spies on Dorothy, and eventually enters his own violent sexual relationship with her, stepping out of the role of hero and into something more ambiguous.

The way the violence is portrayed in Blue Velvet , and the fact that a man directed it, would seldom fly for a major studio in 2026. Yet despite being “problematic” through today’s more rigid ethical lens, it may be one of the most important pieces of cinema ever made. Its refusal to offer easy answers is what makes it a masterpiece. By forcing the audience to inhabit Jeffrey’s perspective, it explores complicity and darkness lurking in ordinary people, ultimately exposing the rot beneath the sheen of suburban America. 

Without Blue Velvet proving that surrealist art-house horror could captivate a mainstream audience, Lynch might never have gotten the chance to make later masterworks like Twin Peaks and Mulholland Drive . His pieces have inspired everything from The Sopranos to Atlanta to Severance . While it may be easy to dismiss a film based on rigid moral rules, it’s important to remember that how characters behave in stories isn’t a reflection of the director’s own stance. Rather, these are fictional explorations of difficult topics that help us make sense of the nonsensical world around us.

articles.title: Did Anyone Have a Better 2012 Than Chris Hemsworth? After 14 Years, the Answer May Be No
articles.summary: In 2026, everyone knows Chris Hemsworth since he's one of the biggest movie stars around. His run as Thor in the Marvel Cinematic Universe has lasted well over a decade, he has been an important part of several other notable franchise films like Men in Black: International and Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga, and he's […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google In 2026, everyone knows Chris Hemsworth since he's one of the biggest movie stars around. His run as Thor in the Marvel Cinematic Universe has lasted well over a decade, he has been an important part of several other notable franchise films like Men in Black: International and Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga , and he's a beloved staple of Hollywood. Of course, there was a time when he was still relatively unknown and looking to break out, which is how we got his stellar opening scene in 2009's Star Trek , where he nearly stole the show.

That performance helped him land his role as the God of Thunder in the MCU, starting with 2011's Thor . As good as he was there and as well as that film performed at the box office, it was still going to take a lot for Chris Hemsworth to become a household name. To that point, Thor was the actor's only true starring role, but that was slated to change in 2012. Hemsworth was part of four movies that were pretty big in their own right, from a big-budget superhero film to a new adaptation of an iconic fairy tale to a remake of a classic war flick to one of the best horror comedies ever made.

It's not uncommon for actors to star in four films in one year, but it is rare for each of those movies to be at least somewhat impactful. That's what makes Chris Hemsworth's 2012 so spectacular and why nobody had a year like him. It started with the smallest role of the four, as Hemsworth was part of the cast of The Cabin in the Woods . Despite not being a major hit, it went on to become a modern cult classic and showed the world just how hilarious Hemsworth could be. In fact, comedic timing remains one of the best elements of Hemsworth's acting talents and The Cabin in the Woods was the first look at it.

The biggest hit for Hemsworth of 2012 came next as he reprised his role as Thor in The Avengers . It grossed over $1 billion and revealed how well he works in an ensemble cast. Thor is often at his best when he gets to play off his co-stars, which was evident there. Next, Hemsworth played Eric the Huntsman in Snow White and the Huntsman , which is an action take on the fairy tale . Again, we saw how versatile Hemsworth could be and how great he is when working alongside a strong cast of actors.

His final film of 2012 was the least successful, as Red Dawn is a remake of the 1984 war movie of the same name. It flopped commercially and didn't receive the strongest reviews, but Hemsworth's work was praised. It might not be his best effort but it helped cement him as a star. The only other star who had an argument for having the best 2012 is Jennifer Lawrence, who started her run in The Hunger Games franchise and had an Oscar-winning turn in Silver Linings Playbook . As great as that was, it's hard to beat what Hemsworth did and how that impacted his stardom as there aren't many actors who have had better careers since 2012 than him.

Do you have any other actors from 2012 who might've had a better year than Chris Hemsworth? Let us know in the comments.

The " You Can See Everything " phenomenal has landed in the U.K. with historic results.

A24 's monster documentary about Theranos fraudster Elizabeth Holmes — which has already amassed more than $90 million in the U.S. after just after 5 weeks in cinemas — has now enjoyed the biggest British opening weekend ever for a non-concert doc.

articles.title: Star Wars Finally Answered Empire Strikes Back's Weirdest Scene Six Years Ago, And It's Canon
articles.summary: In May 1980, Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back flew into theaters to great excitement. The second film in what would become the original trilogy, many viewers were left with questions after one strange scene. As the Empire began to overpower the Rebel Alliance, Luke Skywalker (Mark Hamill) went to Dagobah to train with Jedi […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google In May 1980, Star Wars : The Empire Strikes Back flew into theaters to great excitement. The second film in what would become the original trilogy, many viewers were left with questions after one strange scene. As the Empire began to overpower the Rebel Alliance, Luke Skywalker (Mark Hamill) went to Dagobah to train with Jedi Master Yoda (Frank Oz) after the spirit of Jedi Master Obi-Wan Kenobi (Alecc Guinness) told him to. Yoda, elderly and in hiding on Dagobah, reluctantly accepted him as his apprentice. Yoda trained Luke to master the light side of the Force and avoid turning to the dark side like his father, Jedi Anakin Skywalker turned Dark Lord of the Sith Darth Vader .

As part of his training, Luke was sent into a cave. While inside the cave, Darth Vader appeared. The two engaged in a brief battle, and it ended with Luke killing Darth Vader by removing his head with his lightsaber, which then tumbled to the ground. The face of the helmet broke away to reveal Luke's face. Obviously, none of this was real. But what could have caused this strange vision within the cave? That question was finally answered in 2020, 40 years later.

On November 10, 2020, From a Certain View: The Empire Strikes Back was published by Del Rey as part of the iconic film's 40th anniversary celebration. The book, which is part of a series expanding on all three films in the original trilogy for their 40th anniversaries, contains a set of 40 anthologies set during the time period of The Empire Strikes Back . Canon to the film, each story was written by a different author and recreated an iconic scene from the film. But this time, those scenes were shown from the perspective of a supporting character. One told the story of a naturalist caring for tauntauns on the icy planet Hoth. Another told the story of the tauntaun that was cut open to keep Luke warm.

The short story "Vergence" by Tracy Deonn told the story of the Cave of Evil, also known as the dark-side cave. The cave was a vergence, a naturally occurring area of Force energy. These areas give Force-sensitive individuals greater interaction with the phenomena and can even cause visions. The Cave of Evil was fueled by the dark side of the Force, which led to anyone who entered seeing visions of their greatest fears. Miraculously, it somehow developed somewhat of a consciousness as well. In an effort to learn the path to eternal consciousness, Yoda entered the cave and was confronted with visions of what would later become Order 66. While in exile on Dagobah, Yoda would regularly visit the cave to confront his fears. His light side powers also helped balance out the cave's dark side powers, preventing its influence from spreading throughout the planet. Before Luke arrived, Yoda went into the cave one last time to face his guilt and fear of failure, readying himself for the task ahead.

The End of the Evil Image courtesy of Lucasfilm Part of the story tells the origins of the cave and Yoda's connection to it. Another part reveals its fate. After Yoda died and became one with the Force in Return of the Jedi , there was nothing left to balance the dark forces oozing from the Cave of Evil. It was able to expand its influence across the entire planet of Dagobah. Many years later, Luke Skywalker's nephew Kylo Ren (Adam Driver) and his master Snoke (Andy Serkis) traveled to the swamp planet. Entering the cave, he experienced visions of Luke, along with his parents, Princess Leia and Han Solo.

He was able to kill the vision of Luke, but not his parents. To cover up the fact that he couldn't do so and hide what would be perceived as a weakness, he destroyed the Cave of Evil. Snoke was unhappy with him for doing so, as he had hoped to bring other apprentices there to test them, but Kylo Ren assured him he would never need another apprentice. But this would prove a blessing for the rest of Dagobah, as they were finally free from the influence of the Cave of Evil.

What do you think of the Cave of Evil's origin story? Let us know in the comments.

articles.content:
Five films made using Google Flow, an AI creative workspace from Google, by filmmakers based as far apart as Kerala and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands have won the inaugural WIF India x Google Flow Filmathon and will screen Monday at the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa.

Women in Film India (WIF India) ran the Filmathon with Google Flow to give emerging filmmakers around the country a chance to tell stories with AI tools. Women made three of the five winning films. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Blackpink's Jisoo Signs With WME for Worldwide Representation Blackpink's Jisoo Gets Early Release Window on Tencent Music as Revenue Rises 5.6% to $1.3 Billion

The organizers set out to put filmmaking tools within reach of more people and to find storytellers working outside India's established production centers. The open call attracted more than 850 registrations. Of the entries, 60% came from Tier 1 cities, 30% from Tier 2 cities and 10% from Tier 3 cities.

"Every major technological shift in filmmaking brings with it an opportunity to rethink who gets to make films, whose stories find an audience and whose perspectives shape the medium," said Guneet Monga Kapoor , founder and CEO of WIF India. "It is vital that women are at the center of that conversation, not on the periphery of it. Seeing three of the five selected films come from women filmmakers is particularly encouraging."

Two of the winners come from Kerala. Aswathi Naduthodi, from Calicut, made "Bombay Mumbai – Vada Pav," a visual essay that charts decades of change in Mumbai through people whose lives connect to the city's best-known street snack. Kochi-based Syam Manohar's "Kuli" is a Tamil-language black comedy in which an outsider digging a strange hole sets off a spiral of gossip in a sleepy village. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

From Port Blair in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Promita Banerjee's "Sikkal" is a Hindi folk-horror piece about guilt and grief in which a man is haunted by apparitions of his dead sister. Mumbai filmmaker Nikhil Shinde's "Pedals of Joy" is an animated Hindi tale of brotherhood, built around a young balloon vendor who longs for a sports bike.

Delhi's Srishti Chaudhary made "Nazar," an animated film with no dialogue that relies on visual metaphor to deal with the burden of the unwanted gaze. Chaudhary designed the film's character sheets and storyboards inside Google Flow.

"India has no shortage of compelling stories or people with the imagination to tell them. What has historically been missing is equal access to the tools and opportunities that can bring those stories to the screen," said Rabia Chopra, WIF India's director of programs and development. "You shouldn't need an expensive camera, an industry network or even a formal filmmaking background to have a voice in cinema."

A seven-member jury chose the winners. It comprised directors Shakun Batra and Pan Nalin, editor Nitin Baid, editor and director Deepa Bhatia, film and streaming executive Aparna Purohit and Google Envisioning Studio's Prashant Paulose, along with Sten Saluveer, who heads Cannes Next at the Cannes Film Market.

"The five finalists powerfully demonstrate how Google's AI creative studio can expand a filmmaker's artistic horizon, elevating their craft while ensuring that human imagination remains the undisputed heart of the narrative," said Arathi Sethumadhavan, director, international activations and product insights, technology and society, at Google.

The Entertainment Society of Goa and the Government of Goa are backing the IFFI showcase, which gives the five filmmakers a chance to show their AI-assisted work to a broad industry audience at one of the country's top national film events.

WIF India has positioned the results as part of a larger goal: making sure women help decide what cinema looks like as new technology changes how films get made.

A new trailer is expected to drop later today that is guaranteed to have some information that has been otherwise missing until now, which will surely fill us in on who else we can expect to join the fight against Doctor Doom as well as who will be joining the Latverian despot in his conquest. All roads lead to Secret Wars , but we've got a lot of work to do until we get there.

Recent additions to Doomsday's characters include a possible appearance by Vision (if Anthony Mackie is a reliable source which he has not yet proven to be) and Bucky in a new outfit . Many familiar faces have been confirmed to be in the movie for some time, such as Steve Rogers' return and The Fantastic Four, but we may have one other unexpected teammate for the good guys who just shocked everyone with their announcement.

Hailee Steinfeld broke the internet when Marvel Studios and Disney Animation collaborated on an Instagram post to promote the upcoming release of a different movie, Hexed . However, the video featuring the actress took a swift turn into a jaw-dropping direction, as Steinfeld revealed a gift she received from The House of Mouse that wasn't what she or the audience thought it was going to be. Without saying more than a sentence, Steinfeld announced her next role to the surprise of many fans.

"I'm here with my movie Hexed ," she explained in the video, "but it looks like they delivered a chair from a different movie." Behind her, a director's chair wrapped in a green and black ribbon — the signature color palette for Doomsday . Accompanying the video was a simple caption that read “Catch Hailee Steinfeld in Disney’s Hexed before she returns in Avengers: Doomsday .”

View this post on Instagram Steinfeld's last appearance in the MCU was during a post-credit scene in The Marvels from 2023, where Kate Bishop encountered Kamala Khan as she began recruiting for a team of her own, the Young Avengers. Prior to that, she introduced the character during the Disney+ Hawkeye series from 2021, along with reprising the purple-clad archer in a non-canonical episode from What If…? Viewers of Sony's animated Spiderverse series know her best as Gwen Stacy from Earth-65 AKA Spider-Gwen, a character many were hoping she would bring to life in the MCU but will have to wait a little bit longer for that collab to happen.

Bishop's involvement in the film began in September when a SCREENX trailer revealed several scenes that had never been shown before , including one of Scott Lang with his daughter Cassie hugging in what eagle-eyed fans realized was Bishop's apartment. While she wasn't actually shown during that trailer, people did the math and realized there was a strong possibility that this character was going to pop up in Doomsday in one way or another. With this surprise social media announcement, we know for a fact that Clint Barton's protege will be letting her arrows fly in the fight against Doom and his minions.

As for Bishop's mentor, Hawkeye will not be appearing in Doomsday , but if his recent post on X is to be believed , Jeremy Renner may be gearing up for a role with a different squad — The West Coast Avengers. One thing we do now about this upcoming saga is that the MCU will get a slight reboot with the changing universe. A team like this would definitely mix things up in a great way, but we have to see who survives Doomsday and Secret War first before we get too hyped up about this rumor.

articles.title: 4 '90s Classics That Need a Legacy Sequel After Home Alone, And One Also Stars Macaulay Culkin
articles.summary: Home Alone is finally back, as it has been announced that Chris Columbus' 1990 Christmas classic is getting a modern-day legacy sequel. The film will bring back Macaulay Culkin as Kevin McCallister, with the film following a now-adult Kevin as he struggles to connect with his own son. It's great that Home Alone is getting […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Home Alone is finally back, as it has been announced that Chris Columbus' 1990 Christmas classic is getting a modern-day legacy sequel. The film will bring back Macaulay Culkin as Kevin McCallister, with the film following a now-adult Kevin as he struggles to connect with his own son.

It's great that Home Alone is getting a legacy sequel, but it is far from the only '90s classic that deserves one. So, here are four franchises from the '90s that should come back for another go-around, with legacy sequels that could appeal to all audiences.

Home Alone turned Macaulay Culkin into one of the biggest child stars of the 1990s, and only a few years later this title was solidified with the release of 1994's Richie Rich . Based on the comic book character of the same name, Richie Rich stars Culkin as the world's richest boy, who must foil a plot by the CFO of Rich Industries to kill the Rich family and steal their fortune.

The Richie Rich franchise could easily come back in the modern day, with Culkin returning as an adult Richie. The premise for the original film is pretty simple, so a legacy sequel could take the concept in a variety of directions. An easy way would be to introduce Richie's kid, with Culkin's character having to raise a child who acts exactly how he used to. On the other hand, the film could also be a satire of the presentation of wealth, with an adult Richie Rich being used to lampoon real-life billionaires and trillionaires.

Sam Raimi's 1990 horror superhero film Darkman is rated R. However, it was viewed by many kids of the '90s, and it is doubtful that the film would get the same rating if it were released today. The film follows a scientist, played by Liam Neeson, who develops a synthetic skin that disintegrates after 99 minutes. However, his journalist girlfriend gets in trouble with the mob, causing organized criminals to break into the lab and disfigure him. Presumed dead, he uses his synthetic skin and the enhanced strength he received as a result of his nerve damage to become Darkman, a shapeshifting superhero who seeks revenge on the criminals who ruined his life.

Raimi is still working today, with 2026's Send Help proving that there is still an audience for the director's original works. Plus, Liam Neeson is still a massive actor, with him even headlining The Naked Gun , an action comedy that was released in 2025. So, a new Darkman movie definitely needs to happen , even if 2026's Clayface stole the original film's thunder. Plus, after two direct-to-DVD sequels with Arnold Vosloo as Darkman, it'll be nice to see Neeson finally return to the role.

Jim Carrey was one of the biggest stars of the 1990s, and one of the actor's most popular films was 1994's The Mask , directed by Chuck Russell. Based on the Dark Horse Comics series of the same name, the film follows Carrey as Stanley Ipkis, a cartoon-obsessed bank teller who finds a magical mask created by the Norse god Loki. When he puts on the mask, he becomes a reality-warping super being, using cartoon logic to fight criminals and change the world around him.

Surprisingly, The Mask hasn't gotten a modern legacy sequel, as the film is still incredibly popular today. While the 2005 sequel Son of the Mask definitely tainted the franchise, a new film starring Carrey could redeem it. Whether the movie is a true successor to the 1994 original or a darker take more in line with the source material, the range that Carrey has developed over the past few decades means that he could pull it off. The Mask 2 needs to happen , even if convincing Carrey to come back may be the hardest part.

If you're looking for another 1990s film like Home Alone , it's hard to find one more similar than Gore Verbinski's 1997 comedy classic Mouse Hunt . The film stars Nathan Lane and Lee Evans as two brothers who inherit a mansion that they discover was built by an incredibly famous architect. Hoping to sell it, they begin fixing up the house. However, they must first get rid of a mouse. While the task seems simple, the duo must resort to increasingly complex and ridiculous means to rid the residence of the rodent.

Mouse Hunt 's cartoon logic and slapstick humor are incredibly unique, with the film essentially being a live-action Looney Tunes movie. A legacy sequel would be simple to pull off, as it would just need to follow two more characters trying to kill a mouse. The original film ends with Lane, Evans, and the mouse living in harmony, but it would be fun to see their characters come back, with them warning the new protagonist about the dangers that come with trying to hunt a mouse.

What '90s classic do you want to see get a legacy sequel? Let us know on the ComicBook Forum !

articles.title: 40 Years Ago, a Cult Director Made One of the Best Lovecraftian Horror Movies of All Time
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Empire Pictures It has been 40 years since a beloved cult director and his leading actor set out to make an H.P. Lovecraft short story into a movie that became an instant cult classic. In 1920, Lovecraft sat down and wrote the horror short story "From Beyond," a tale that was first published 14 years later in […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google It has been 40 years since a beloved cult director and his leading actor set out to make an H.P. Lovecraft short story into a movie that became an instant cult classic. In 1920, Lovecraft sat down and wrote the horror short story "From Beyond," a tale that was first published 14 years later in a magazine called The Fantasy Fan . The story was told from the first-person point of view of an unnamed narrator who had experiences with a scientist named Tillinghast, a man who created a device that helped people see outside the scope of accepted reality. The alternate dimension it reveals is full of murderous monsters that attempt to get into our world. It is the type of Lovecraftian horror the author helped create.

Director Stuart Gordon and actor Jeffrey Combs set out to turn this H.P. Lovecraft short story into a movie, and on October 24, 1986, From Beyond was released into theaters. While the movie was a box office flop, it received decent reviews and has gone on to become a beloved cult classic for horror fans.

From Beyond Delivers a Perfect Lovecraftian Horror Experience Image Courtesy of Empire Pictures In From Beyond , Ted Sorel stars as Dr. Edward Pretorius, a hedonistic and ambitious scientist who creates a machine called the Resonator that allows him to see beyond our reality. It is the same idea as in the short story, but what happens at the end of the short story, when the monsters invade our world, happens at the beginning of the movie. A creature from the alternate dimension bites his assistant, Dr. Crawford Tillinghast (Jeffrey Combs), and then Pretorius, mad with power, turns the machine up to full power and ends up dying by decapitation. Crawford is then arrested for his murder.

The movie then follows Crawford as he begins to mutate into something otherworldly. He meets a doctor named Katherine (Barbara Crampton) and is accompanied by a detective named Bubba Brownlee (Ken Foree), who is investigating Pretorius' death. They return to the lab, and when Crawford turns the machine back on, the creatures come back, including Dr. Pretorius, whose consciousness is now altered and part of the other world. From there, the movie becomes a Lovecraftian body-horror nightmare.

The movie cost Gordon $2.5 million to make, but it only brought in $1.3 million at the box office. However, it still received positive reviews, with a 73% critics score on Rotten Tomatoes and a 70% audience rating. The critics' consensus on Rotten Tomatoes reads, " From Beyond stands as a stunningly grotesque Lovecraft adaptation with a dazzling blend of chilling effects and brainy, cosmic horror."

Stuart Gordon specialized in experimental horror , and it was clear throughout his entire career that H.P. Lovecraft was his biggest influence. Just as Sam Raimi created his movies with Bruce Campbell by his side in the lead roles, Gordon had Jeffrey Combs by his side most of the time. The two are as interconnected as Raimi and Campbell, but their work was so offbeat that they never had the same crossover success as Raimi and Campbell, though their movies all stand as cult classics, especially for people who love cosmic horror.

From Beyond is the second of his collaborations with Combs and horror legend Barbara Crampton (who also starred in Re-Animator ). It was, in fact, his splatter masterpiece Re-Animator that made him a horror icon. Just like From Beyond , Re-Animator was also based on an H.P. Lovecraft story, a serial novelette called "Herbert West — Reanimator." Once again, this was a cosmic body-horror film. But this was about bringing the dead back to life, and how that was never a smart idea. Just like in From Beyond , a scientist who tried to play God ended up falling in the end.

Both movies also share the trait of using Lovecraft's stories as a launching pad rather than the template for the movies. With the foundation laid by Lovecraft in his stories, Gordon was able to create something new and fresh, while still maintaining the themes and ideas that the master sci-fi author built into his stories. From Beyond goes even further than Re-Animator . While Re-Animator was a gross-out horror tale , From Beyond just throws the goopy creatures at the audience and turns the scientist Pretorius into something beyond words. It is body horror that eclipses anything David Cronenberg was doing at the time, at least as far as gross-out effects are concerned. It is also bitingly funny, which is where Gordon was able to really shine, making his Lovecraftian horror movies unlike any other in the subgenre.

Have you seen From Beyond ? Let us know your thoughts on this Lovecraftian horror movie in the comments below.

articles.title: I Love Star Trek: The Next Generation but Deep Space Nine Blew It Out of the Water
articles.summary: Star Trek is in a rough place right now, but this isn't the first time and it almost certainly won't be the last. The Original Series only lasted three seasons, with the last one being mostly blah. The fanbase kept it alive, which would allow creator Gene Roddenberry to bring it back as films (although […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Star Trek is in a rough place right now, but this isn't the first time and it almost certainly won't be the last. The Original Series only lasted three seasons, with the last one being mostly blah. The fanbase kept it alive, which would allow creator Gene Roddenberry to bring it back as films (although he did try to get it as a new show), starting with Star Trek: The Motion Picture . The movies were successful and a return to TV came in 1987 with Star Trek: The Next Generation . This show brought the classic franchise into the modern day and despite a rough first season ( Trek first seasons can be pretty blah), the show would become a success. For many fans, it's their favorite Trek , but for others of us, there's another – Star Trek: Deep Space Nine .

The Next Generation was classic Trek – monster of the week episodes that allowed us to dig into our cast, as well as lore episodes that would call back to other moments in the series. It was a great show, but it was just like everything else on TV at the time. However, Deep Space Nine was 21st century TV in the '90s. It took the franchise in new directions, showing that Trek didn't just have to be one thing. Star Trek is full of brilliant episodes , and some of the best of all-time come from TNG . However, Deep Space Nine was able to blow it out of the water by taking Trek in all new directions.

Before we go on, I just want to impress something upon you – I am not in any way saying that Star Trek: The Next Generation is bad. I was 6 when it started and watched it every week (Sundays at 7:00pm on channel 44) until it ended. It's an amazing show, with characters that it was easy to love. It was a smart show that rewarded its viewers and was a great recipient of the legacy of Star Trek . However, it was still rather limited by its format. The writers tried to add serialization to the show, but it never really worked. The first season tried to set up the Romulans and Ferengi as the main villains, as well as introduce the admiralty conspiracy, but none of these plots ever came to fruition.

Star Trek: Deep Space Nine went in a completely different direction. The Next Generation was set on the flagship of the fleet, commanded by a erudite ambassador of a man and staffed by the best of the best. DS9 took place in the armpit of the galaxy, with the Cardassian occupation of Bajor seeing the aliens abandon their ore-processing station Terek Nor . Renamed Deep Space Nine , the Federation is asked to run the station, leading to the discovery of the wormhole to the Gamma Quadrant.

That was the premise of the show, but it was also so much more than that. Avery Brooks played Commander Benjamin Sisko. Sisko took part in the Battle of Wolf-359, when Picard as Locutus destroyed 39 Starfleet ships, losing his wife. DS9 was his last stop before he was contemplating retiring. The discovery of the wormhole – and the non-linear aliens known as the Prophets, the gods of the Bajoran people – change his life, as he learns he is the Emissary of the Bajoran people.

Deep Space Nine 's cast is the perfect blend of misfits. There's Major Kira, the former Bajoran freedom fighter first officer, Jadzia Dax, the 800-year old Trill science officer who knew Ben when she was a man, Odo, the shapechanging constable, Dr. Julian Bashir, the bright-eyed, ladies' (lizards', too) man chief medical officer, Chief Miles O'Brien, the transporter chief from TNG , the only noncom Starfleet officer with a name, and the most tormented officer in the fleet, Ben's son Jake, the Ferengi bar owner Quark, his brother Rom, and nephew Quark, and the plain, simple Cardassian tailor Garak, a delightful person who knows everything from gardening to murder. Worf would join later in the show, bringing General Martok and the Klingons, and the show had the best Trek villains in Cardassian Gul Dukat and Winn Adami, the twisted Bajoran Kai.

These characters were the key to the show. Benjamin Sisko wasn't Captain Picard – as proven by his tango with Q – and DS9 wasn't TNG . Each of the characters had complicated pasts that would often come roaring to the fore, and the show was able to build them into fully-realized characters over its seven-year run. Even Ezri Dax, who joined in the last season, got well-fleshed out. The show also dug deeper into the Ferengi, showing more of their hyper-capitalist society, introduced one of the most interesting Trek races ever in the Cardassians and their sad fascism, and was able to make the Star Trek Universe actually feel like it was a real place and not just a series of planets of the week.

The first two seasons were about establishing this new corner of the universe and the characters, and they did a fantastic job. In fact, DS9 has the best two seasons in Trek history. The rest of the show would deal with the war with the Dominion, showing us a side of the Federation we had never seen before. Not only did we get to see them in combat, but we also got to see how they dealt with losing, as much of the war went against them. It also introduced the coolest ship in Star Trek – Sisko's strong right hand, the U.S.S. Defiant NX-74205 (look, I love the Akira -class too, but you know I'm right).

Star Trek: The Next Generation is a better old school sci-fi show, but Deep Space Nine feels more like a modern show . The serialization paid off, allowing the writers room to create something unique in the pantheon of the franchise. It has the strongest acting in the series, which is what happens when you put talent like Brooks, Andrew Robinson, Nana Visitor, Marc Alaimo, Louise Fletcher, Alexander Siddig, Terry Farrell, Colm Meaney, Armin Shimmerman, Max Grodenchik, Aaron Eisenberg, J.G. Heltzger, and so many others together on a soundstage. It changed Star Trek forever and remains a favorite of fans and critics alike.

The 21st century has been an amazing time for TV, whether it be prestige or genre. People started to look at TV as a legitimate storytelling medium, to the extent that for many, TV shows beat the pants off movies. The Golden Age of TV grew out of the '90s and shows like Star Trek: Deep Space Nine paved the way for it. Sure, it was just a Star Trek show, but it was also so much more. It was an example of what you could do when you treated the sci-fi genre – and its fans – with respect.

I have many fond memories of TNG , but I was older when DS9 started. The show grew up with me and it helped me to learn to appreciate storytelling and character more. Sci-fi is one of the most versatile genres out there and DS9 showed that it could be more than just fun weekly fluff. It showed that it could be dark and intelligent, taking the lessons of Treks past and creating the perfect Star Trek .

What do you think about Star Trek: Deep Space Nine ? Do you like it more than The Next Generation ? Sound off in the comment section below.

articles.title: Spain Pitches Incentives, Crews and a 500 Million-Strong Spanish-Speaking Market to India at WAVES Film Bazaar
articles.summary: Spain, the Country of Honor at this year's International Film Festival of India (IFFI), made its case to Indian filmmakers at WAVES Film Bazaar in Goa, laying out its incentives, locations and crews and pushing for closer co-production ties. articles.content:
Spain , the Country of Honor at this year's International Film Festival of India (IFFI), made its case to Indian filmmakers at WAVES Film Bazaar in Goa, laying out its incentives, locations and crews and pushing for closer co-production ties.

The panel, "Spain: Where Stories Find Their Stage – Incentives, Locations & Co-production Opportunities," was part of the Knowledge Series at the 20th edition of the market, which runs Nov. 20-24 alongside the 57th IFFI. Variety Asia editor Naman Ramachandran moderated. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Rich Eisen's 'Beautiful Day': Landing All Four Members of U2 as Guests The Game Awards Adds Disney+ to Livestream Lineup

"For us, co-production is a key instrument," said Camilo Vázquez, deputy director of the Institute of Cinematography and Audiovisual Arts (ICAA), the film agency of Spain's Ministry of Culture. He pointed to better financing, exchanges between technical and artistic teams, and stories that could connect with audiences in both countries, and described the timing as particularly favorable for India-Spain partnerships.

For Indian producers weighing Spain as a filming destination, the offer extends beyond its locations. Usha Jadhav, a National Award-winning actor and producer with Spanish company ACortes Films, highlighted the country's track record with international productions, its range of landscapes and architecture, and skilled crews used to working on both big-budget and independent films. She also cited eight-hour shifts and quieter shooting environments as practical advantages, particularly for sync-sound productions.

Jadhav said the relationship should not be limited to service work, and made a case for collaborations that bring creative teams together across borders. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"Language is not a barrier, because cinema itself is a universal language," Jadhav said. "We need human stories."

Lara Molina, general coordinator of the Spain Film Commission, outlined the tax incentives available to international productions. Miguel Fabián Salazar, Spain's economic and commercial counselor in Mumbai for the country's trade and investment agency ICEX, set out what each side brings. India offers production scale, a large consumer market, a global diaspora and strengths in VFX and animation. Spain offers experienced crews, creative talent and access to Europe and Latin America. Partnerships could run from co-production and financing to distribution, post-production and production services.

"These points somehow fit together. They are not exclusive. They all feed into each other," Salazar said, noting that Spanish films and productions were traveling farther internationally while Indian productions and streaming services were growing fast.

ICEX's Mumbai office works with producers and distributors on market access, local partnerships, setting up businesses and regulatory requirements. It has also organized business missions involving Indian companies in animation, post-production and gaming.

For Indian producers looking to develop a project with Spanish partners, Guillermo Rodríguez, director of the Valladolid-based cultural institution Casa de la India, said: "The real roadmap is about building connections and building trust."

India and Spain signed their audiovisual co-production agreement in 2012. Rodríguez said the scheme was being updated and that clear guidelines would be issued.

"If you plan to shoot in both countries or one of the countries, you have to make sure you follow those guidelines precisely. Under the co-production agreement, an Indian producer has to approach NFDC… and the Spanish co-producer has to go to ICAA," he said.

NFDC is India's National Film Development Corporation.

The session closed with a showcase of five Spanish projects seeking Indian collaborators. These included "My Parents Grand Bazaar," the feature debut of Andalusian filmmaker Rakesh Narwani; "Serendipia," an India-Mexico-Spain romance; "The Dragon Letter," from Ladakh-born director Stanzin Jigmet, based on his short of the same name, which won gold in the narrative category at the 2026 Student Academy Awards; animated project "Mumu"; and documentary "Aana and Aai – The War to Become an Artist." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Rodríguez noted that the two countries had largely stuck to familiar markets, with Spain looking toward Europe and Latin America and India toward English-speaking territories.

"Imagine the global Indian industry working with the Spanish-speaking world," he said. "Because Spain is not just Spain. It's access to the entire Spanish-speaking world – over 500 million people. So if you can bring those two cultural superpowers together, imagine the potential."

articles.title: Clayface Streaming Release Date Revealed as the $30 Million Film Passes the DCU’s Biggest Bomb at the Box Office
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Warner Bros. Only 45 days after its theatrical release, Clayface is coming to digital with an announced release date of December 8. This is a pretty big deal, as the movie is still thriving at the box office, making more money, which has ensured it is profitable thanks to the lower budget that James Gunn set so […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Only 45 days after its theatrical release, Clayface is coming to digital with an announced release date of December 8. This is a pretty big deal, as the movie is still thriving at the box office, making more money, which has ensured it is profitable thanks to the lower budget that James Gunn set so it could be a success as an offbeat comic book horror movie. Clayface tells the story of an actor named Matt Hagen, who was disfigured by the local mafia. When he agreed to an experimental procedure, he became the supervillain Clayface and sought revenge.

Clayface hits digital on December 8, which is a pretty normal wait for a horror movie like this. While movies like Superman had a longer run in theaters as big-budget spectacle releases, films like Clayface become available a lot quicker because of the niche genre. This announcement also came the same weekend that Clayface passed the $126 million mark at the box office, coming close to surpassing Supergirl's total .

CLAYFACE takes shape on Digital December 8th. Over 45 days after its theatrical debut 🫠 pic.twitter.com/kvTnVKMBbv

On the same weekend that the Clayface digital release was announced, Clayface was still rolling along in its theatrical run . It passed the $126 million mark at the worldwide box office. Superman made $618.7 million on a $225 million budget. Supergirl only made $126.5 million on a $170 million budget, taking a huge loss at the box office. Knowing a horror movie would make less money, James Gunn produced Clayface on a low $40 million budget, which makes its current box office take of $126.2 million a clear profit. The film will pass Supergirl this week.

That is a big deal because it proved that James Gunn knew what he was doing when setting up Clayface for its release, ensuring it was able to make a profit thanks to the lower budget. This didn't make up for the loss that Supergirl experienced, but that was a special case where it started off at a disadvantage. It is also important to note that this will probably be the last time DC releases a movie anything like Clayface , since the new people in charge are not likely to take chances on properties like this and will focus solely on the big-name characters from now on.

For fans who loved what Clayface offered, though, it will arrive in just a few short weeks on digital and allow people to have the movie at home to enjoy. It shouldn't take long after that for it to arrive on HBO Max, and the Blu-ray and 4K release will probably come in January, since it takes an average of anywhere from two weeks to eight weeks to receive a physical release after the digital.

articles.title: A $1.8 Billion Action Fantasy Epic Has Sailed to Streaming Success and It Would be a Tragedy Not to Watch It
articles.summary: Courtesy of Universal Pictures There have been many epic stories told based on Greek myths and legends. Many of them have become huge box office successes thanks to the fascination with tales of monsters and heroes from a time long forgotten, and that includes one of the biggest movies of the decade. Released earlier this year in competition with […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google There have been many epic stories told based on Greek myths and legends. Many of them have become huge box office successes thanks to the fascination with tales of monsters and heroes from a time long forgotten, and that includes one of the biggest movies of the decade. Released earlier this year in competition with summer blockbusters like Spider-Man: Brand New Day , Christopher Nolan followed up his Oscar-winning Oppenheimer with probably his most unexpected project today a mega-budget retelling of The Odyssey . After making a huge profit in cinemas - despite an equally massive budget - Nolan's biggest film to date has now arrived on PVOD and instantly dominated several streaming platforms hosting the movie including Apple Store and Amazon. Despite millions turning out to see the star-studded spectacle in theaters, it seems that just as many are now watching it at home and you probably should watch it too if you haven't seen it yet.

The Odyssey is a story that has been told many times over the last century, in TV shows and on the big screen. However, there have been few versions like Christopher Nolan's retelling, which does for Greek myth what he did for Batman and bring a gritty grounded feel to a story full of wonder and fantasy. The story of Odysseus making his dangerous journey home after the Trojan War includes plenty of action, fearsome monsters, and converging storylines that bring The Odyssey to life like never before with some of the biggest actors in Hollywood right now filling a stacked cast. Matt Damon plays Odysseus, and he is ably helped by Tom Holland, Anne Hathaway, Jon Bernthal, Zendaya, Charlize Theron, Robert Pattinson, Lupita Nyong'o and more. Of course, it would not be a Christopher Nolan movie without backing up this talented cast with some kind groundbreaking filmmaking process and Nolan did not disappoint in this either.

Christopher Nolan's love of movies is well-documented, so it came as no surprise that the director wanted to make The Odyssey with the final cinematic experience in mind. This resulted in him capturing his movie entirely on IMAX film cameras, a first for any film and a task that used over two million feet of 70mm film to make Nolan's vision a reality. While many of those watching in regular cinemas were not able to appreciate this extra effort, The Odyssey took over the vast majority of IMAX screens around the world on its release, meaning there were a lot of cinefiles and Nolan fans able to experience the film with the breathtaking scale he intended. The takeover of IMAX cinemas, with its higher ticket prices, did not hurt when it came to pushing the movie's box office total to $1.8 billion worldwide.

Nolan's record-breaking run did not stop with the making of the movie. The movie gave Nolan his highest ever opening weekend gross, surpassing the $248 million of The Dark Knight Rises with a total of $264.1, as well as being the highest grossing R-rated movie, Universal Pictures' movie, and Nolan-directed film. For a movie seen by many as a huge gamble, and one that generated plenty of forthright opinions on social media for several casting decisions, it paid off massively for everyone involved. Additionally, it continued Nolan's streak of highly praised films, earning a 94% RT score, making it Nolan's best reviewed movie. Now that the film is available at home on PVOD services, many who decided to skip The Odyssey in cinemas are discovering the towering achievement by Nolan that begs the question of what he can possible do to top it. Will he follow it up with The Iliad as fellow director Steven Spielberg has suggested? We can only wait and see, but after The Odyssey 's massive success Universal would probably have no issues greenlighting the movie if Nolan chose to do it.

Would you like to see Nolan return to Greek myth again for his next movie? Have you seen The Odyssey yet? Let us know in the comments.

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google It seems that one Avengers: Doomsday star has hinted at when people might expect to see the final trailer for the upcoming Marvel Cinematic Universe movie. There has been a lot of talk about the next trailer for the movie, and there are even hints that it will be an incredibly emotional trailer, which suggests it will show a lot more than the past trailers. So far, there have been teasers that hinted at who was going to be in the movie, a bigger trailer that showed the heroes planning to fight Doctor Doom, and the most recent one focused on Doom with more of a look at Captain America.

It seems like Simu Liu has teased the upcoming arrival of the next Avengers: Doomsday trailer. This came from two posts on his Instagram Stories. The first had an emoji of a clock set to 10:10, and the second had a winking face. This has led people to believe that the new Avengers: Doomsday trailer will finally arrive on Monday, and this is something that most MCU fans have been waiting for.

Simu Liu is seemingly teasing the final trailer for ‘AVENGERS: DOOMSDAY’ via Instagram: “🕰️😉” pic.twitter.com/aiUEvpTPtT

The new Avengers: Doomsday trailer, expected to hit on Monday, was previously teased by Hayley Atwell , who plays Peggy Carter in the MCU. With Simu Liu now hinting at its arrival, it seems that what Atwell teased might be coming as early as tomorrow morning. This will likely give a lot more footage of Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom, but the idea that it might be an emotional trailer makes it seem like there will be a lot more shown concerning possible deaths or even the end of certain worlds.

Remember, Avengers: Doomsday is based on the Marvel Comics storyline "Time Runs Out," which saw the incursions destroying every Earth in the multiverse, an event that counts down to only two Earths remaining. From the look of it, those two Earths might be Earth-616 with the Avengers and the X-Men's Earth, which is where the original Fox X-Men cast is returning, along with some fun additions like Channing Tatum's Gambit showing back up again after his appearance in Deadpool & Wolverine . There are also rumors of other Earths, including Tobey Maguire's Spider-Man Earth. Could the emotional footage be showing something like Maguire's Earth being destroyed?

There is also the chance that the emotions could come from the death of someone important being shown in the trailer, and the idea that it could be Patrick Stewart's Professor X could be something that could devastate audiences. Honestly, it will probably not show any of that, with Marvel saving the surprises, deaths, and destruction for the movie itself. Instead, it might play into the feelings people have for the old X-Men and Spider-Man movies , and how this could finally end those stories for good. Whatever it is, Simu Liu makes it seem like Monday will be when the trailer drops.

articles.title: Marvel Heroes Are Having an Identity Crisis, and It's About More Than Secret Identities
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics If you've been reading modern Marvel, there's one storyline that's been recurring multiple times across numerous comics. Superheroes keep having their identities stolen in one capacity or another. This has become especially prevalent with some of the heroes' most iconic villains, with prominent examples being Norman Osborn temporarily taking over as Spider-Man without Peter's permission […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google If you've been reading modern Marvel , there's one storyline that's been recurring multiple times across numerous comics. Superheroes keep having their identities stolen in one capacity or another. This has become especially prevalent with some of the heroes' most iconic villains, with prominent examples being Norman Osborn temporarily taking over as Spider-Man without Peter's permission and the Eldest stealing the Hulk's body in the pages of Infernal Hulk . On the surface, this doesn't appear to be anything out of the ordinary, as heroes are plenty known to share similar stories across the board, but this goes far deeper than simple circular and mirrored storytelling.

This is actually a reflection of a major change in how Marvel treats its superheroes. When they were first created, the vast majority of them were meant to embody the world-outside-your-window perspective, being portrayed as more down-to-earth and less paragon-esque than DC's heroes were in the Silver and Bronze Ages. That's continued to this day, to some extent, but that barrier has been breaking down steadily over decades. Nowadays, Marvel's heroes are ideals given human form, and the reason villains keep taking their faces is to explicitly relate to how important the heroes have become to us.

Back in the 1960s, Marvel sought to differentiate itself from DC by offering a different type of hero. The vast majority of DC's catalogue at the time was taken up by paragons who could do no wrong, from Superman to Wonder Woman to Batman. Their stories were often simplistic, and thus their ideologies were often portrayed the same way. Marvel challenged that by grounding its heroes in the then-modern day with deeply personal struggles. Think of the family drama inherent to the Fantastic Four or Spider-Man's efforts to balance making rent with his superheroic duties. This resulted in heroes who felt rougher around the edges, in a way. They made more unjustifiable mistakes than DC's heroes did.

However, it didn't stay that way forever. Over time, Marvel started portraying its heroes in a more traditional DC way, while DC's own heroes took on deeper, more human flaws. Spider-Man is a perfect example . In his earliest years, Peter was a brash, abrasive young man who had a chip on his shoulder the size of Texas. Yet, as he did more and more heroics, that part naturally faded away. Modern portrayals of Peter, even when they tackle the start of his career, portray him as the wiser, more centered hero that he's become. You could accuse this of Marvel sanitizing Peter in some way, and that may be a part of it, but the reason that this happens across the board is that these heroes have come to mean something much more to fans over the years.

The moments that stick with the most fans the most are when heroes are at their most heroic. Spider-Man pushing past his limits to save Aunt May. Hulk choosing to forgive the Leader and himself. These moments are noble and heroic in their truest sense, so as the hero continues to develop, these moments and interpretations stick when other aspects don't. Repeated moments like this have elevated the heroes from characters who tried to be heroic to the very faces of what it means to embody those ideals. They've become more and more like paragons, more and more like modern myths meant to inspire. Which brings us to why so many villains want to take those heroes' identities.

The supervillain stealing a hero's identity storyline has become a true epidemic. In the past few years alone, it's happened to most of Marvel's biggest names. The Edlest has taken the Hulk's body, Norman impersonated Spider-Man, Grant Rogers is back to pretending to be Captain America, and more. This idea of someone else becoming a hero has expanded to an entire subgenre, including different takes on it like A.I.M. attempting to make their own Tony Stark, not Iron Man, and Beta Ray Bill grappling with the reality of everyone thinking he was Thor after the God of Thunder was erased from existence. It's going on across the board, and the answer isn't as simple as villains wanting to abuse everyone's faith in these heroes. Rather, it's an examination of what these heroes stand for.

This happens to Cap , Spider-Man, and Hulk more than anyone else, and there's a reason for that. The first two are the de facto paragons of Marvel, representing the peak of the heroism all others strive to emulate. The Hulk, meanwhile, has always served as a window into the inner rage and anguish that a person could go through, and how working through that or living with it could work. These three are ideas just as much as they are characters, which makes them perfect to contrast against others who steal or borrow their names.

Whenever someone steals one of these superheroic identities, the story itself serves as an argument of what it is that makes that person a hero. We look through all of their choices and actions, and come to the conclusion that these characters have risen to the ranks that they have because they always attempt to do the right thing. By juxtaposing the hero's success to how these villains fail to live up to those standards or miss the point, it highlights how special the heroes are. They have fully transitioned from being characters to being something greater, and there's no better way to show that than by direct comparison.

Marvel's writers have been exploring the place heroes have in the world not as individuals, but as ideas to strive for. Spider-Man is someone who struggles but always puts being responsible over personal gain. Captain America is a man who will never stop fighting for liberty and equality. These characters mean something more to people, and thus they are being treated more as myths and explorations of what people wish to be over standard protagonists. Simply put, Marvel's heroes have been constantly getting more heroic, and the best way to dissect that is with villains who show us everything that the heroes aren't.

articles.title: 5 Invincible Universe Characters I'm Still Waiting to See in the Prime Video Series
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Image Comics Invincible is coming back for a fifth season, and while the comics paint a pretty good picture of what will happen in the coming episodes, several things are still up in the air.
