articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Invincible is coming back for a fifth season, and while the comics paint a pretty good picture of what will happen in the coming episodes, several things are still up in the air. After all, the Prime Video series has already made a ton of changes to the Image Comics run, with season 4 even introducing an original storyline centered around Damien Darkblood.

With a teaser for Invincible season 5 now released , the show's return is finally starting to feel close. So, ahead of season 5's premiere on February 17, 2027, here are five characters from the Invincible comics that I can't wait to see make their debut in the animated series. WARNING: Contains spoilers for the Invincible comics .

One of the only characters we know will debut in Invincible season 5 is Gravitator. Gravitator is a street-level villain whose real name is Chris, a factory worker who began his criminal career so that he could buy an engagement ring. So, he builds an anti-gravity suit and robs a bank, although he is caught in the act by Invincible. After a couple of missteps and another encounter with Invincible, Mark realizes that Chris has the potential to be a good person. So, he puts him in contact with the GDA, where Chris goes on to work.

Jack Quaid has been cast as Gravitator in Invincible season 5 , and it'll be incredibly exciting to see the actor take on another superhero role. Quaid rose to popularity due to his role as Hughie in Prime Video's adaptation of The Boys . However, he has also proven himself to be a talented superhero voice actor thanks to his title role in My Adventures with Superman .

If Markus Murphy does appear in Invincible , it probably won't be in season 5. After all, the character makes his debut in issue #129, while season 4 wrapped up with the reveal that the Viltrumites have assimilated to Earth in the wake of the Viltrumite War, which occurs in issue #77. So, season 6 seems like a more likely time for Markus to make his debut. However, it is possible that a scene directly linked to Markus' first appearance may occur in season 5, if it happens at all.

In the comics, Markus is the son of Mark Grayson. He was conceived after Anissa, the Viltrumite villain who has already appeared several times throughout the series, sexually assaulted Mark in an attempt to continue the Viltrumite bloodline. This is one of the most controversial scenes from the comics, and since the Prime Video series has avoided some of the source material's controversial subjects, it'll be interesting to see how Invincible handles the Anissa and Markus storyline.

In Invincible season 4, Robot and Monster Girl enter the Flaxan Dimension in order to save Earth by closing the Flaxan portal. However, they become stuck on the other side, with them ending the season trapped in a universe where time occurs much faster. Season 5 will undoubtedly continue this storyline , which is one of the most interesting ones from the Invincible comics. Thus, it wouldn't be surprising for season 5 to feature the debut of Monster Girl's son, Monax Zaxal.

After spending decades in the Flaxan Dimension, Robot manages to overthrow the alien government and rebuild Flaxan society. Throughout the years, Robot's increasingly authoritarian actions cause Monster Girl to resent him, with her eventually leading a rebellion against his rule. While they are apart, Monster Girl and another Flaxan have a child named Monax. Eventually, Monax makes his way to Earth, with him seeking revenge on Robot.

Terra Grayson is arguably the most significant Invincible comics character who hasn't appeared in the show yet, and I can't wait for her to make her debut. As the daughter of Mark and Atom Eve, Terra is gifted with all the powers of a Viltrumite, immediately making her one of the most powerful characters in the Invincible universe. Terra makes her debut in issue #113, and while she probably won't be present in season 5, it is likely that the upcoming episodes will set the stage for Terra to appear in the following season.

Terra is key to many of the later Invincible stories, and she will become increasingly important as the series nears its end. Since so much of Invincible so far has been about the relationship between Nolan and Mark, it'll be interesting to see how the show handles putting Mark in the parental role with Terra. There are tons of interesting themes that could be explored with this storyline, and it'll add another layer to the world of Invincible .

It is a near-guarantee that we will see all of the aforementioned Invincible characters before the Prime Video series ends. Spawn, on the other hand, has already missed his opportunity to show up. Created by Todd McFarlane, Spawn is the most iconic Image Comics superhero, with him having a 1990s HBO animated series and a 1997 live-action feature film. After dying, going to Hell, and making a deal with a demon, the hero is brought back to Earth as a Hellspawn, where he attempts to atone for his past sins by fighting evil.

Spawn appears in the Invincible comics as an Image Comics crossover character, with him showing up during major events like the Invincible War. Initially, no characters who originated outside of Invincible appeared in the Prime Video show, with them being replaced by other Invincible heroes and villains. However, seasons 3 and 4 have featured previously missing crossover characters, like Tech Jacket, Brit, and the Astounding Wolf-Man. Unfortunately, Spawn has still been left out of the series . While television rights are probably behind Spawn's exclusion, I hope Prime Video manages to pull off a cameo before Invincible ends.

Which Invincible characters are you still waiting on? Let us know on the ComicBook Forum !

articles.title: 6 Great Crime Films to Watch When You Eventually Need A Break From GTA VI
articles.summary: It is impossible not to have heard about the release of Grand Theft Auto VI, as gamers across the globe are now playing one of the most highly anticipated video games of all time. Rockstar's newest release has received critical acclaim and is currently claiming hours of attention from anyone who has purchased it. No […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google It is impossible not to have heard about the release of Grand Theft Auto VI , as gamers across the globe are now playing one of the most highly anticipated video games of all time. Rockstar's newest release has received critical acclaim and is currently claiming hours of attention from anyone who has purchased it.

No matter how incredible the game is, a binge session can only go so long. Eventually, fans are going to want a break. Luckily, these six crime films will scratch the same itch as GTA VI , keeping viewers in the zone before they drop back into Vice City.

Michael Mann's 2004 film Collateral is one of the greatest movies of the 2000s, and it still holds up nearly two decades (and several GTA games) later. The film follows Jamie Foxx's Max Durocher, a Los Angeles cab driver who is given an incredibly high fare to drive to several locations with Tom Cruise's Vincent. Eventually, Max discovers that Vincent is a hitman, making the driver an accomplice to his crimes. So, Max must play his cards right in order to survive the night, escape Vincent, and avoid any trouble from the fallout of the killings.

Collateral has all of the key elements that make a GTA game, such as automotive crime, violent killings , and a seedy criminal underworld. The film takes place in LA, which is parodied in the GTA V setting, Los Santos. Plus, GTA VI actually references Collateral , as players can have an encounter where an NPC inspired by Vincent takes Jason hostage and forces him to drive a taxi around. So, before getting to this moment in the game, it's a good idea to check out Collateral .

This isn't the first or the last time that a Michael Mann film will appear on this list, but 1995's Heat is arguably the director's best film , and it fits perfectly into the vibe of GTA VI . Set in Los Angeles, the film follows the cat-and-mouse game between Al Pacino's LAPD detective Vincent Hanna and Robert De Niro's aging career criminal Neil McCauley. The near-three-hour epic kicks off with an iconic sequence in which an armored car is robbed, and the ball doesn't stop rolling until the credits.

Heat features intricately planned, large-scale robberies and a cast of criminal characters, and it's not hard to see how the film inspired the GTA franchise. On top of that, the film hinges on a tense chase of a cop trying to catch a criminal. Much of the fun of the GTA games is trying to help your criminal player character evade the police, and while Heat is a bit more dramatic, it perfectly captures this conflict.

Directed by Ridley Scott, the mastermind behind Alien and Blade Runner , 1991's Thelma & Louise is one of the director's most underrated films. The film stars Geena Davis as Thelma and Susan Sarandon as Louise, two friends who decide to go on a weekend fishing trip. While on the way, the duo kills an attempted rapist at a bar. So, they decide to flee to Mexico, with them driving their 1996 Ford Thunderbird convertible across the country as the FBI pursues them. The film was critically acclaimed, with it being nominated for six Oscars and winning Best Original Screenplay. Tragically, the film hasn't received the same mainstream notoriety as some of Scott's franchise films.

Like some of the other films on this list, Thelma & Louise is about characters running away from the police. However, the chase is far more literal in this film, as the police are always just one step behind the duo. Like in GTA , the main characters have to evade police cars and helicopters, and they occasionally have to survive encounters with the authorities while keeping their identities hidden.

Released only a year before Jaws , 1974's The Sugarland Express is one of legendary director Steven Spielberg's lesser-known films. However, it is just as good as any of the filmmaker's other masterpieces. The film stars Goldie Hawn as Lou Jean and William Atherton as Clovis, the latter of whom begins the film incarcerated. Lou Jean pays Clovis a visit to inform him that their son will soon be placed in foster care. So, they steal a car, take a police officer hostage, and go on the run from the authorities as they attempt to reach their son.

Players of GTA VI should immediately be able to see the parallels. Like The Sugarland Express , GTA VI follows a criminal couple who, after one of them gets out of prison, attempt to regain custody of their young child. Both the film and the game feature a massive amount of police vehicles getting involved in chases, and a world of crime centered around a surprisingly tender relationship.

When it comes to movies centered around a police chase, it is impossible to think of one more iconic than Hal Needham's 1977 film Smokey and the Bandit . The film follows two criminals, Burt Reynolds' Bo "Bandit" Darville and Jerry Reed's Cledus "The Snowman" Snow, who are tasked with illegally transporting a large supply of Coors beer from Texarkana to Atlanta for some wealthy benefactors. Knowing that law enforcement will be on their tail, they devise a plan. Snowman will drive the truck full of beer, while the Bandit will act as a blocker, using his iconic 1977 Pontiac Trans Am to distract police. However, they never could have expected how persistent Jackie Gleason's Sheriff Buford T. Justice would be.

Smokey and the Bandit is a film about transporting an illegal drug while evading law enforcement by way of reckless driving. It is hard to think of a film that could be more GTA than that. Plus, the film's Southern setting makes it not too far off from GTA VI 's South Florida setting, with the film's cast resembling some of the side characters in the game.

Michael Mann is a master of the crime genre, and no film from throughout cinematic history could be a better companion piece to GTA VI than the director's 2006 take on Miami Vice . Based on the iconic 1980s TV show, Miami Vice stars Colin Farrell as Sonny and Jamie Foxx as Rico, two officers from the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office who work together to take on the world of illegal narcotics.

Miami Vice is all over the DNA of GTA VI , with the game's setting even paying tribute to the franchise by being named Vice City. The game's blue and pink color scheme is directly ripped from the original show, and while this isn't as present in the 2006 film, it occasionally pops up. A game based on GTA VI would feel exactly like Miami Vice , and until one gets made, this is the closest to a GTA movie adaptation that we have.

What crime movies remind you of GTA ? Let us know on the ComicBook Forum !
